title: Position the piezo disc sensor (offboard)
description: Place the piezo disc to the left of the breadboard, not inserted into it. The disc floats freely — its two leads (red = signal, black = GND) will connect to the breadboard via jumper wires. Do not push the disc pins into any breadboard holes.

title: Place the 100k series resistor
description: Insert the 100kΩ resistor with one leg in hole 10a (same bank as the piezo signal row but separate net) and the other leg in hole 14a. This resistor sits inline between the piezo signal and the analog input. It protects the ADC from voltage spikes that piezo discs can generate.

title: Place the 1MΩ bleed resistor
description: Insert the 1MΩ bleed resistor with one leg in hole 14b and the other in hole 18b. The 14b hole is in the same breadboard row as 14a (the output of the series resistor), so both resistors share the signal node without an extra wire. The far end (18b) will be tied to GND.

title: Wire piezo signal lead → series resistor input
description: Run a red jumper wire from the piezo disc's red lead (pin 'plus') to breadboard hole 10e. The wire-end anchors directly to the disc pin, so the cable runs freely from the disc to the breadboard where it lands on the same row as the 100k series resistor's input pin (10a).

title: Wire signal node → Bela / Arduino analog input
description: Run a green jumper wire from breadboard hole 14d to the Bela analog input pin 0 (or Arduino A0 on the stand-in board). Hole 14d is in the same row as 14a (series R output) and 14b (bleed R input), so all three share the same signal net automatically.

title: Wire piezo ground lead → GND rail
description: Run a black jumper wire from the piezo disc's black lead (pin 'minus') directly to any hole on the top negative power rail. The cable runs freely from the disc to the rail — no breadboard row is needed for this connection.

title: Wire bleed resistor GND end → GND rail
description: Run a black jumper wire from breadboard hole 18d to the top negative power rail. This completes the DC bleed path from the signal node to ground.

title: Wire Bela / Arduino GND → GND rail
description: Run a black jumper wire from the GND pin on the Arduino Uno (or Bela GND header) to the top negative power rail. This ensures the board and piezo share a common ground reference — essential for a valid analog reading.

title: Verify signal path
description: Trace the signal path before powering on: Piezo plus lead → red wire → breadboard row 10 → R_series (10a→14a) → row 14 signal node (shared with R_bleed pin1 at 14b) → green wire (14d→A0). Bleed: row 14 signal node → R_bleed (14b→18b) → black wire (18d→GND rail). Ground: piezo minus lead → black wire → GND rail ← Arduino GND pin.

title: Bela board substitution note
description: On the real build, replace the Arduino Uno with the Bela board. Connect the signal wire (green) to Bela analog input header pin 0 (channel 0). Connect the black GND wire to any Bela GND header pin. The Bela ADC is 12-bit with 0–4.096V range; the signal node at ~4.5V is just above this — consider reducing the series R to 47k if you need the full dynamic range on very hard strikes.
